summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: most Hindi videos get roughly 1,000-1,400 views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly get under 60 views. The best videos use a surprising 'it doesn't X, it actually Y' framing about a familiar sensor or robot (gyro robot, clap switch, IR robot) and earn likes, saves and shares. Generic 'How does X work?' titles, newer videos with no Instagram push, and videos not posted to Instagram at all (many early ones) get very little.
winningPattern: Hindi, a relatable sensor or robot (robot balance, clap switch, IR obstacle sensor, DHT11, mic) with a myth-busting hook such as 'X doesn't do A, it only does B' or a 'why does this happen?' curiosity gap. Short Hinglish titles with one emoji and #shorts, published on Instagram Reels first, where reach is 1,000+. Robot and clap-switch topics also pull YouTube views (400-680). Shares spike on 'surprising fact' or 'did you know' type topics (soil sensor: 24 shares, IR robot: 10).
doMore: Post every video to Instagram Reels as well as YouTube; 8 of the 9 videos with no Instagram numbers got under 30 views overall.
Make more robot-behaviour videos (falling, avoiding walls, following lines) with a visible demo in the first 2 seconds.
Use the myth-busting title: 'Sensor X doesn't do A, only B' about everyday devices.
Make follow-ups on winners, such as a clap switch part 3, a gyro robot part 2 and an IR robot part 2, since series topics repeat well.
End with a save/share prompt like 'Save this for your next project', since saves and shares signal strong interest.
stopDoing: Stop plain textbook titles like 'X Kaise Kaam Karta Hai?' and 'X Fire Kaise Sense Karta Hai?', which consistently underperform.
Stop publishing near-duplicate topics (4 smoke, tap and clap variants) within days of each other; they split the audience.
Stop mixing in English videos for now; the one English upload got 161 views with no Instagram push, so test it separately later.
